body: bus adopted as step 0; mailbox still read once per cycle

cycle 6: reflex stalled 34min holding its lock; every 5-min invocation early-returned at 'previous reflex still at work' WITHOUT logging, so Last Result=0 and the last log line both read healthy. Only the mtime was wrong, and nothing watches mtime. Fix: log the skip (one line), plus the mtime>15min alarm I proposed in cycle 2 -- it catches both this and the crash case. Also run() default timeout 2400s > lock staleness 1500s, so two runs can overlap; those two numbers are the wrong way round. Full report: monitor/inbox/20260728T143836Z-opsm-reflex-stalls-are-invisible.md . Good news: a4a-ablation-build logged 'gates: ablation-arm' -- the tree-derived gate ran 5 suites on the very merge that introduced them, no table edit needed. Full gate 15/15 green. Zero flags, zero manual merges this cycle.

cycle 6 addendum: the git-add-A sweep happened AGAIN, second time today. Commit a24e899 (author engine-rig, titled for A4a's PARTNER_SYNC entry) swallowed all four of my staged files along with its own 51-line PARTNER_SYNC change. My content landed intact this time so damage is zero -- but note the 12:40Z fix was scoped to the monitor only, and this actor was a different session. The hazard is fleet-wide: ANY session committing at repo root with add -A/. can capture another's staged work, and last time it captured ci_merge.py mid-edit and shipped a merge gate that ran zero tests. Suggest the explicit-paths rule go into ALL.md and CHARTER as a fleet rule, not a monitor habit. My own mitigation from now on: 'git commit -- <paths>' in one step, which removes the staged-but-uncommitted window entirely rather than relying on everyone else behaving.
